executive_summary.headline: The system works, but it carries serious risks that should be handled before any new feature.

points.text: spring-web 5.3.39, a library the system depends on, has publicly known security flaws.
Part of the system runs on Spring Framework 5.3.39, which its maker stopped fixing on 2024-08-31.
spring-webmvc 5.3.39, a library the system depends on, has publicly known security flaws.
A small set of files absorbs most of the changes and most of the risk.
Within a year, Java will stop getting security fixes.
spring-context 5.3.39, a library the system depends on, has publicly known security flaws.

executive_summary.recommendation: Recommended path: replatform — Upgrade runtimes and frameworks that are past end of life, keeping the architecture. The system is built on Jakarta EE, MyBatis, Spring.

options.summary: Keep the system as it is and only fix what is urgent (secrets, known vulnerabilities).
assumptions: Team of 3 developers familiar with the stack
Risk keeps growing while the platform ages

options.summary: Move the same application to new infrastructure (containers or cloud VMs) without changing its code.
assumptions: Team of 3 developers familiar with the stack
Size: about 9 thousand lines of code
Ranges are ±50% and come from size and findings, not from a detailed plan
Runtime can be containerized or installed on new servers

options.summary: Modernize gradually behind the same interfaces (strangler pattern), starting with the hotspots.

options.summary: Rebuild on a new architecture, reusing the business rules found in this report.

faq.question: Is the system at risk today?
faq.answer: Yes. The first items in the risk list should be handled now.

faq.question: Can we keep it as it is?
faq.answer: Only for a short time: keeping it means accepting the risks above.

faq.question: How long would the recommended path take?
faq.answer: About 5–11 weeks for a team of 3, plus the first two roadmap phases. These are ranges from the size of the code and the findings, not a commitment.

faq.question: What should we do first?
faq.answer: Phase 0 of the roadmap: close exposed secrets and known vulnerabilities, and get builds running automatically.

faq.question: How sure are these findings?
faq.answer: All 6 findings are verified by tools (manifests, git history, scanners). Each one links to its evidence.
